question_text:
A cylindrical rod 120 mm long and having a diameter of 15.0 mm is to be deformed using a tensile load of $35,000 \mathrm{~N}$. It must not experience either plastic deformation or a diameter reduction of more than $1.2 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~mm}$. Calculate the change in diameter of the candidate materials.

| Material | Modulus of Elasticity (GPa) | Yield Strength (MPa) | Poisson's Ratio |
| :-- | :--: | :--: | :--: |
| Aluminum alloy | 70 | 250 | 0.33 |
| Titanium alloy | 105 | 850 | 0.36 |
| Steel alloy | 205 | 550 | 0.27 |

Give your answer as a tuple (Aluminum alloy,  Steel alloy, Titanium alloy).The units of each required answer are (mm, mm, mm), respectively.
response:
## Solution

**1. Compute the tensile stress** (uniform, same for all materials):

$$A_0 = \pi\left(\frac{d_0}{2}\right)^2 = \pi(7.5)^2 = 56.25\pi\ \text{mm}^2$$

$$\sigma = \frac{F}{A_0} = \frac{35000}{56.25\pi} \approx 198.06\ \text{MPa}$$

**2. Check plastic deformation** (σ must be < yield strength):

| Material | σ (MPa) | Yield (MPa) | Plastic? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Aluminum | 198.06 | 250 | No |
| Titanium | 198.06 | 850 | No |
| Steel | 198.06 | 550 | No |

All remain elastic, so $\varepsilon = \sigma/E$ (Hooke's law) applies.

**3. Diameter change** from Poisson contraction:

$$\varepsilon_{\text{lat}} = -\nu\,\varepsilon = -\nu\frac{\sigma}{E}, \qquad \Delta d = \varepsilon_{\text{lat}}\,d_0 = -\nu\frac{\sigma}{E}d_0$$

| Material | E (GPa) | ν | Δd (mm) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Aluminum | 70 | 0.33 | −0.0140 |
| Steel | 205 | 0.27 | −0.00391 |
| Titanium | 105 | 0.36 | −0.0102 |

(Note: Aluminum's reduction 0.0140 mm exceeds the 0.012 mm limit, so it would be disqualified on the diameter-reduction criterion — but the question asks only for the calculated change in diameter.)

$$\boxed{(-0.0140,\ -0.00391,\ -0.0102)}$$
